products.title: Bougainvillea
products.description: A vibrant flowering shrub or climbing plant known for its colorful, papery bracts in shades of pink, purple, orange, red, and white. Bougainvillea adds dramatic color to sunny gardens, balconies, and patios, thriving in warm conditions with plenty of direct sunlight.

symbolism.origin: Named after French explorer Louis Antoine de Bougainville, this colorful ornamental plant is admired for its vivid bracts and vigorous growth. Its bold appearance inspires associations with hospitality, passion, and joyful celebration.

growing_instructions: Plant in a well-draining potting mix and use a container with drainage holes if growing in a pot.
Provide at least six hours of direct sunlight daily for healthy growth and abundant flowering.
Keep outdoors in a sunny, sheltered location during warm weather, but protect from frost and freezing temperatures.
In Kashmir, move container-grown plants to a bright, protected, frost-free location before winter temperatures drop sharply.
Allow the soil to dry partially between waterings. Avoid excessive moisture, especially during cool weather.
Prune lightly after flowering or as needed to control growth, and wear gloves because the stems may have sharp thorns.
care_instructions: Water thoroughly when the upper layer of soil has dried, allowing excess water to drain away.
Reduce watering during winter when growth slows, while preventing the root ball from remaining excessively wet.
Use a balanced or flowering-plant fertilizer according to the label during active growth, avoiding excessive nitrogen that encourages foliage over flowers.
Remove dead or damaged branches and trim overly long shoots to maintain the desired shape.
Inspect periodically for aphids, mealybugs, and scale insects, and maintain good airflow around the plant.

products.title: Caladium
products.description: A classic Caladium cultivar with large heart-shaped leaves featuring brilliant white centres and bold green margins and veins. Native to tropical South America, this tuberous plant is prized for its dramatic foliage contrast.

growing_instructions: Start tubers indoors in April or plant outside in late May after all spring frost risks have passed.
Vibrant foliage display peaks from June through September in warm, humid shade.
Cannot survive Kashmir's sub-zero winter; dig up tubers before frost in October and store dry indoors at 15°C.
Tubers remain completely dormant underground from November through March.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: Native to the Amazon basin, its heart-shaped leaves splashed in crimson and white give it the folk names 'Heart of Jesus' and 'Angel Wings', symbolizing deep joy and divine protection.

products.title: Cherry Pepper (Wiri Wiri)
products.description: Compact ornamental pepper plant with small, round, cherry-like peppers in vibrant colors. Highly ornamental with attractive foliage and colorful fruit. Prolific producer of mild to moderately hot peppers.

growing_instructions: Start seeds indoors in March or transplant container seedlings outdoors in May after final spring frosts.
Vegetative growth and white flowers peak from June to July in warm valley sunshine.
Ornamental cherry peppers turn brilliant glossy scarlet and harvest from August through October.
Plants succumb to early Kashmir freezes in November; harvest mature peppers and collect seeds beforehand.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: Cultivated for both vibrant culinary heat and vivid ornamental beauty; in folk traditions, ornamental chili peppers ward off bad fortune and inspire lively passion.

products.title: Cycas Palm (Young)
products.description: A slow-growing, ancient cycad with a sturdy trunk and glossy, feather-like evergreen fronds. Adds a sculptural, tropical look to indoor spaces, patios, and sheltered gardens. Toxic if ingested; keep away from pets and children.

symbolism.origin: Cycads are an ancient lineage of seed plants that existed long before modern flowering plants. Their longevity and enduring form inspire associations with resilience, permanence, and timeless strength.

growing_instructions: Grow in well-draining soil enriched with gritty material. Use a pot with drainage holes to prevent waterlogging.
Place in bright, filtered light or partial shade, protecting foliage from harsh afternoon sun when acclimating.
Keep outdoors only during frost-free weather in Kashmir. Move to a bright, sheltered indoor space before temperatures approach freezing.
Water thoroughly when the upper soil has dried, allowing excess water to drain. Reduce watering during winter and avoid keeping the soil constantly wet.
care_instructions: Use a well-draining potting mix and avoid standing water around the roots.
Feed sparingly with a balanced fertilizer during active growth, following the product label.
Remove only dead or damaged fronds; healthy green fronds support the plant's growth.
Inspect periodically for scale insects, mealybugs, and spider mites.
Keep away from children and pets. All parts of Cycas revoluta are toxic if ingested, particularly the seeds.

products.title: English Ivy
products.description: An evergreen climbing plant with glossy green leaves, ideal for covering trellises, walls, hanging planters, and shaded garden areas. Vigorous and easy to maintain, it also works well as groundcover.

symbolism.origin: In Greek and Roman traditions, ivy was associated with Dionysus and enduring bonds. Its evergreen foliage and clinging growth have long made it a symbol of fidelity, steadfast friendship, and lasting affection.

growing_instructions: Plant in well-draining soil during spring or autumn, choosing a location with partial shade or filtered sunlight.
Allow climbing stems to spread along a suitable trellis or support, or let the plant trail from a container.
English ivy tolerates cold conditions once established, but protect potted plants from severe frost and freezing winds in Kashmir.
Trim excessive growth in late winter or early spring to control its spread and maintain the desired shape.
care_instructions: Water when the upper layer of soil begins to dry, adjusting frequency for weather, container size, and drainage.
Use a balanced fertilizer sparingly during active growth if needed.
Remove dead, damaged, or yellowing leaves and trim overgrown stems as required.
Inspect periodically for spider mites, scale insects, and aphids.
Wear gloves when pruning if your skin is sensitive. Keep away from children and pets, as the foliage and berries are toxic if ingested.

products.title: Fern
products.description: Lush, delicate fern with feathery fronds. Thrives in shade and humidity. Adds tropical elegance to indoor spaces and shaded gardens.

growing_instructions: Divide rhizomes and repot in moist, humus-rich soil in mid-spring from April to May.
Graceful arching fronds unfurl rapidly through summer from May to September in cool, moist shade.
Potted ferns require heated indoor shelter away from freezing winter drafts from November to March.
Growth slows from December to February; mist fronds to counteract dry indoor heater air.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: In European and Celtic folklore, the mysterious seedless reproduction of ferns led to myths of invisibility and magic; in Victorian floriography, ferns symbolize sincerity and humble grace.

products.title: Fir
products.description: An elegant evergreen conifer with needle-like foliage and a naturally graceful form. Fir trees add year-round greenery, texture, and structure to gardens and landscapes. Best suited to outdoor planting in cool climates, with adequate space for mature growth.

growing_instructions: Plant in well-drained soil in a location with good light and sufficient space for the tree to mature.
Plant during suitable mild weather, such as spring or early autumn, while avoiding waterlogged or frozen ground.
Water regularly while the young tree establishes, keeping the soil moist but never waterlogged.
Most suitable fir species tolerate cold conditions, but hardiness varies by species and young plants may need protection from drying winds and severe exposure.
Choose the permanent planting location carefully, as many fir trees eventually grow much taller and wider than nursery specimens.
care_instructions: Check soil moisture and adjust watering according to rainfall, temperature, and drainage rather than following a rigid schedule.
Apply a light layer of organic mulch around the root zone, keeping it clear of the trunk.
Use compost or a suitable fertilizer sparingly when needed, following soil conditions and product instructions.
Avoid routine pruning; remove dead or damaged branches when necessary and preserve the natural growth form.
Monitor for scale insects, aphids, and signs of root or needle disease, and address problems early.

symbolism.origin: As evergreen trees that retain their foliage through winter, firs are commonly associated with endurance and continuity. Their persistent greenery inspires symbolic associations with renewal, protection, and stability.

products.title: Garden Palm
products.description: Graceful palm with feathery fronds. Creates tropical ambiance. Hardy variety suitable for indoor and outdoor cultivation.

growing_instructions: Repot into fertile, aerated compost in late spring during April or May.
Active fan frond development takes place from June through August in sheltered sunny spots.
Sensitive to prolonged valley snow and freezing frost; house indoors or in a greenhouse from November through March.
Winter dormancy from December to February requires only light monthly hydration.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: In ancient Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, and Asian traditions, palm fronds were waved in triumphant celebrations and carried as symbols of victory, peace, and sacred hospitality.

products.title: Golden Cypress
products.description: Coniferous tree with golden-yellow foliage. Pyramidal form and warm coloring. Year-round ornamental interest for landscapes.

growing_instructions: Transplant container saplings into garden beds from March to April or October to November.
Vigorous golden-chartreuse foliage development takes place from April through August.
Exceptionally frost-hardy in Srinagar; withstands sub-zero freezes and snow loads without injury.
Lightly trim hedge outline in late February or July; avoid hard pruning into bare wood in winter.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: Coniferous evergreens maintain their lush vitality throughout freezing winters; the bright golden foliage of this cypress represents hope, winter light, and prosperity.

products.title: Green Pine
products.description: Evergreen pine tree with soft green needles. Elegant coniferous form. Excellent for landscaping and creating windbreaks.

growing_instructions: Plant young nursery pines in early spring from March to April before candle extension begins.
New needle candles push strongly across sunny days from April through July.
Native to Kashmir's mountains; completely cold-hardy through severe freezing winters and heavy snow.
Dormant from November to February; brush heavy wet snow off young branches to prevent bending.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: In Himalayan, Japanese, and Chinese traditions, the evergreen pine is the premier emblem of moral fortitude, winter longevity, and an unbending spirit in mountain gales.

products.title: Italian Cypress (Pencil Pine)
products.description: Tall, slender Italian Cypress with dark green foliage. Ideal for formal gardens and Mediterranean landscapes. Requires full sun and well-drained soil.

growing_instructions: Plant columnar saplings in well-drained sunny soil in March-April or October.
Vertical spire growth peaks between May and August in warm valley sun.
Hardy in valley conditions; loosely tie upper spires to prevent splaying under heavy snow from December to February.
Prune errant lateral sprays in late winter in February before spring sap begins flowing.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: Sacred to Pluto in classical antiquity, Italian Cypress has stood as the dignified guardian of Mediterranean and Persian gardens for millennia, symbolizing eternity and architectural grace.

products.title: Japanese Spindle
products.description: Decorative shrub with elegant variegated foliage. Unique fall colors and interesting winged seed pods. Attractive year-round.

growing_instructions: Set out evergreen hedge saplings in March-April or during autumn in October.
Dense glossy foliage pushes actively from April through August.
Fully winter-hardy across Srinagar; easily survives frost and sub-zero temperatures down to -12°C.
Shear hedge lines in late February or mid-summer in July.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: Euonymus japonicus was planted in traditional Japanese and courtyard hedge gardens to signify steadfast protection, companionship, and beauty through all seasons.

products.title: Money Plant (Devil's Ivy)
products.description: Popular indoor money plant (Epipremnum aureum) known for its air-purifying qualities. Easy to grow in pots or hanging baskets.

symbolism.origin: In Vastu Shastra and Feng Shui traditions, Epipremnum aureum is renowned as the primary living magnet for wealth, prosperity, and positive domestic chi.

growing_instructions: Plant or repot in well-drained loamy compost during mild spring weather from April to June.
Active vine expansion occurs from May through September in bright, indirect indoor sunlight.
Tender to Kashmir's freezing winters; keep strictly indoors in heated rooms away from frost and cold window drafts from November through March.
Dormant during winter; reduce watering to once every 10-14 days from December through February.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

products.title: Purple Heart
products.description: A striking ornamental plant with rich purple foliage and delicate pink flowers. Its trailing growth and vivid colour make it ideal for garden borders, containers, hanging planters, and decorative outdoor displays.

growing_instructions: Plant in well-draining soil during spring after the risk of frost has passed.
Provide full sun for the deepest purple foliage, introducing the plant to direct sunlight gradually.
Protect from frost and freezing temperatures in Kashmir by moving potted plants to a bright, sheltered indoor location during winter.
Trim long or leggy stems in spring to encourage compact, bushy growth. Stem cuttings can be used for propagation.
care_instructions: Water when the upper layer of soil begins to dry, allowing excess water to drain freely.
Reduce watering during cold weather when growth slows, and avoid waterlogged soil.
Apply a balanced fertilizer sparingly during active growth according to the product label.
Pinch growing tips and remove damaged or yellowing leaves to maintain a neat appearance.
Inspect periodically for mealybugs, aphids, and signs of fungal problems.

symbolism.origin: Purple Heart, Tradescantia pallida, is admired for its vivid violet foliage and resilient, spreading growth. Its rich colour and enduring appearance inspire associations with dignity, individuality, and perseverance.

products.title: Red Maple
products.description: Elegant Japanese red maple sapling with vibrant red foliage. Thrives in temperate climates. Perfect for gardens and landscapes.

growing_instructions: Plant bare-root or potted saplings in early spring during March or autumn in October.
Fresh leaf growth develops from April to July, followed by brilliant crimson fall foliage in October.
Fully winter-hardy; drops leaves naturally in November and rests dormant through winter cold.
Prune only in late summer or early winter; avoid spring pruning when sap bleeds profusely.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: Celebrated in Asian and North American landscape traditions; the transformative autumn red foliage symbolizes balance, natural harmony, and the peaceful wisdom of passing seasons.

products.title: Rosemary
products.description: Aromatic Mediterranean herb with needle-like silvery-green leaves and small blue flowers. Versatile culinary and medicinal herb with been associated with memory and remembrance since antiquity.

growing_instructions: Transplant saplings into gritty, free-draining garden soil in April or May.
Fragrant needle growth and pale blue flowers peak from May through August.
Moderately frost hardy; mulch root base heavily or protect against severe -5°C snow freezes from December to February.
Prune lightly after summer flowering in August; avoid cutting into old woody stems in winter.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

symbolism.origin: Derived from Latin 'Rosmarinus' (Dew of the Sea); immortalized by Shakespeare ('there's rosemary, that's for remembrance'), it is the historic symbol of fidelity and remembrance.

products.title: Rubber Plant (Large)
products.description: Popular indoor plant with large, glossy, deep green leaves. Excellent air purifier. Grows into a statement piece with minimal care.

symbolism.origin: In botanical lore and Feng Shui, Ficus elastica represents abundance, resilience, grounding strength, and financial stability due to its thick, sturdy, oval leaves.

growing_instructions: Repot into rich, aerated potting soil between April and June as indoor spring temperatures rise.
Foliage expands steadily from May to September in bright, filtered sunlight.
Not frost hardy in Kashmir; maintain indoors at 15°C+ with protection from sub-zero drafts and heater vents from November through March.
Growth slows from December to February; water sparingly only when the top 3 inches of potting mix feel dry.
care_instructions: Water according to species and season: more in summer, reduced in winter and cloudy spells.
Top-dress with compost every 6-8 weeks and remove spent or yellowing foliage.
Prune shape-forming shrubs in late winter before active spring flush.
Monitor for mealybugs, scale, and fungal leaf spots; isolate and treat early.

products.title: Snake Plant
products.description: A striking, upright succulent with stiff, sword-shaped leaves and attractive green variegation. Exceptionally low-maintenance and tolerant of low light, making it a popular choice for homes, offices, and modern interiors.

symbolism.origin: The snake plant, formerly classified as Sansevieria trifasciata and now known as Dracaena trifasciata, is admired for its upright, sword-shaped foliage. Its resilient growth and strong architectural form inspire associations with protection, perseverance, and good fortune.

growing_instructions: Grow in a well-draining succulent potting mix in a container with drainage holes. Repot in spring when the roots become crowded.
Place in bright, indirect light or partial shade. The plant tolerates low light, although growth may be slower.
Keep indoors during Kashmir winters and protect from frost, freezing temperatures, and cold drafts.
Allow the potting mix to dry completely between waterings. Reduce watering considerably during winter when growth slows.
care_instructions: Water thoroughly only when the soil has dried completely, and empty excess water from the saucer.
Avoid overwatering, especially in winter, as waterlogged soil can cause root rot.
Feed sparingly with a balanced fertilizer during active growth according to the product label.
Remove damaged or yellowing leaves at the base using clean pruning tools.
Inspect periodically for mealybugs and scale insects.
Keep away from pets and children, as ingestion can cause gastrointestinal upset.

products.title: Spider Plant
products.description: A popular indoor plant with graceful, arching green-and-white striped leaves. Produces baby plantlets on trailing runners and adds fresh greenery to shelves, windowsills, and hanging planters. Easy to grow and suitable for beginners.

symbolism.origin: The spider plant, Chlorophytum comosum, is admired for its cascading foliage and abundant baby plantlets. These characteristics inspire associations with growth, renewal, nurturing, and abundance.

growing_instructions: Grow in a well-draining potting mix in a container with drainage holes. Repot in spring when the roots become crowded.
Place in bright, indirect light or partial shade. Protect the leaves from harsh afternoon sunlight.
Keep indoors during Kashmir winters and protect from frost and cold drafts.
Allow the upper layer of soil to dry slightly between waterings, reducing watering during cooler months.
Propagate by rooting the baby plantlets that develop on mature trailing runners.
care_instructions: Water thoroughly when the upper soil begins to dry, allowing excess water to drain freely.
Apply a balanced houseplant fertilizer during active growth according to the product label.
Remove brown leaf tips and yellowing leaves with clean scissors.
Inspect periodically for spider mites, mealybugs, and scale insects.
Avoid waterlogging and protect the plant from sudden temperature changes.
